items.headline: Bottega Veneta is back on Instagram
items.caption: After five years of silence, the brand posted a single 'Ciao'.
body: Bottega went quiet on social media in 2021, at the end of Daniel Lee's time as designer.
The silence made the brand feel more exclusive.
How to wear it: one woven Bottega piece, nothing else branded.

items.headline: Burton drops 50 archive pieces on Depop for $50.50 each
items.caption: Fifty years of snowboard style, from neon '70s puffers onward.
body: Burton is marking 50 years with 50 vintage pieces, each priced at $50.50.
The edit spans five decades of snowboard fashion.
How to wear it: a loud vintage shell jacket with plain black trousers.

items.headline: Dr. Martens takes its 'Bouncing Soles' party to Germany
items.caption: Berlin and Munich nights celebrate the AW26 Crazy Horse collection.
body: The name comes from the words stitched on Dr. Martens heel loops since 1960.
The events mixed live music, DJ sets and custom embroidery.
How to wear it: well-worn Docs with straight jeans, scuffs welcome.

items.headline: The Lo Lifes: Polo Ralph Lauren's most devoted fans
items.caption: A reissued photo book on the Brooklyn crew adds a new chapter.
body: The Lo Life subculture began in 1980s Brooklyn, obsessed with collecting Polo.
The 10th-anniversary reissue of 'Bury Me With the Lo On' looks at Polo's influence in prisons.
How to wear it: a big-logo Polo knit with relaxed denim.

items.headline: The 'Royal' Air Jordan 1 returns in OG form
items.caption: Classic blue and black leather, just like the original.
body: Michael Jordan never wore the Royal in an NBA game; ads made it famous.
This version goes back to the original leather upper.
How to wear it: black jeans and a plain white tee.

items.headline: Tommy Hilfiger heads to New York for the holidays
items.caption: A festive campaign in red, white and blue Americana.
body: Tommy's look runs from denim and chinos to sweaters and polos.
The holiday campaign features Aron Piper and other creators in NYC.
How to wear it: a cable-knit sweater over an Oxford shirt.

items.headline: John Pawson: the architect of minimalism
items.caption: A new book from the man behind Calvin Klein's Manhattan store.
body: Pawson designed the Calvin Klein Collections store, London's Design Museum and several monasteries.
His spaces are stripped back to the essentials.
How to wear it: the minimal way: one colour, good fabric, no logos.

items.headline: Huckberry × Marathon's new field watch
items.caption: A rugged 41mm pilot's watch with military roots.
body: Marathon has made watches for the military since 1941.
The CeraShell Navigator is based on a 1986 design for a US Air Force base.
How to wear it: with a waxed jacket and selvedge jeans.

items.headline: A legendary collector is auctioning his rare Cartiers
items.caption: Roni Madhvani built his collection by DMing dealers on Instagram.
body: The Uganda-based collector is known for daring Patek Philippes and funky Cartiers.
He is putting some one-of-one pieces up for auction for the first time.
Style lesson: buy what you love, not what's trending.

items.headline: Tom Hardy's favourite brand makes tough sailing gear
items.caption: ThruDark and Musto team up on hardcore kit for the sea.
body: ThruDark was founded by two former Special Forces soldiers.
Hardy wore its ski jacket in a recent music video.
How to wear it: a technical shell over a knit, even off the boat.

items.headline: The one fragrance Esquire recommends to everyone
items.caption: D.S. & Durga's Cowboy Grass, a cult classic.
body: Esquire calls it a scent that suits almost anyone.
It's a grassy, outdoorsy fragrance from the New York perfume house.
How to wear it: two sprays, not five.

items.headline: A plant-inspired filter catches microplastics in wastewater
items.caption: A first-of-its-kind device is already working in Atlantic City.
body: Princeton alumni designed it to copy water-shedding plants that also attract microplastic particles.
The particles are collected and sent for recycling.
The local utility says removing them is crucial for public safety.

items.headline: Divers rescue a kangaroo found far out at sea
items.caption: A young roo swam over a mile out in South Australia's Boston Bay.
body: A boat crew spotted the exhausted kangaroo and diver Jake Murray scooped it aboard.
Hours later, it hopped away from the beach.
Peak Australia.

items.headline: A stranger secretly pays lunch for 27 people
items.caption: A $420 barbecue bill for disabled residents and carers in Incheon, South Korea.
body: The group from a local welfare centre stopped for lunch after a day of sightseeing.
When they went to pay, a stranger had already covered it.
Small kindness, big day.

items.headline: Apple finally launches a touchscreen Mac
items.caption: The new MacBook Pro gets a touch display, starting at $2,899.
body: It's Apple's first true touchscreen laptop, nearly 10 years after the Touch Bar experiment.
It comes in 14- and 16-inch sizes with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips and up to 128GB of memory.
A new hinge keeps the screen steady when you tap it.
